findings.evidence: The Save button in the project-settings form and the Save button in the notification-settings form both trigger state changes but specify neither loading feedback, success message, nor any indication of the result.
findings.fix: Add a success message or visible control state that confirms the save completed, such as 'Settings saved' or a temporarily disabled Save button that re-enables after feedback.
findings.location: the "project-settings" section, the Save button in the project name form; the "notification-settings" section, the Save button
findings.violation: The artifact triggers state-changing actions (Save) without naming any visible result or confirmation.

findings.evidence: the "invite-sent" section defines 0 controls whose target names another defined state (1 incoming link from elsewhere in the artifact).
findings.fix: Add a control inside the "invite-sent" section whose target is another state the artifact defines, for example a back, cancel, or continue control.
findings.violation: This state offers no control whose target names another state the artifact defines, so a user who reaches it has no path to leave it within the artifact.

findings.evidence: <button> with no text content and no accessible-name attribute
findings.fix: Add visible text to this control, or an aria-label attribute naming what it does.
findings.violation: This control has neither visible text nor an accessible-name attribute, so nothing on screen names what the control does.

findings.evidence: The invite-sent section states 'An invite was sent to the address entered above' but does not repeat or display the actual email address that was invited.
findings.fix: Include the email address in the confirmation message, e.g., 'An invite was sent to user@example.com. It expires in 5 days if not accepted.'
findings.violation: Information needed at this step (the recipient email) is absent; the user must remember it from the previous screen or navigate back.
